tools.name: Nuclei
tools.coverage: Two reviewed GET-only HTTP templates; no redirects/OAST/fuzzing
limitations: Coverage is intentionally bounded; not a complete active vulnerability assessment.

tools.name: OWASP ZAP
tools.command: zap.sh -silent -daemon; protected exact-path context; active rules disabled; sendRequest followRedirects=false; passive alerts
limitations: Unauthenticated responses only; no spider, AJAX spider, active scanning or paid integrations.

tools.name: Burp Suite
limitations: Official PortSwigger download was proxy-blocked (CONNECT HTTP 403) in the assessment environment.
Community Edition has no automated scanner; licensed/manual configuration is required. See security/configs/burp.md.

findings.evidence: The local development response omits X-Content-Type-Options; correct HTML/JSON MIME types were observed. No executable user-controlled response or MIME-confusion attack was reproduced.
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth header omission; practical vulnerability and deployed response behavior remain unverified.
findings.recommendation: Confirm staging headers and MIME behavior, then consider nosniff where compatible. Do not infer production configuration from Vite dev responses.
verification: Agent E manually reviewed the healthy isolated hosted-mode development instance on 2026-10-25.
See security/reports/runtime-assessment.md for scope, evidence and limitations.

findings.description: CSP: Failure to Define Directive with No Fallback
findings.evidence: Observed Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'. src/server.ts appFetch intentionally applies framing protection without a script/style policy; no XSS was reproduced.
findings.impact: A restrictive CSP would limit the impact of a separate injection defect. This scan did not establish such a defect or verify deployed CDN/Worker headers.
findings.recommendation: Verify staging policy and design nonce-aware script restrictions compatible with TanStack bootstrap, Turnstile and PostHog before changing this policy.
verification: Agent E manually reviewed the healthy isolated hosted-mode development instance on 2026-10-25.
See security/reports/runtime-assessment.md for scope, evidence and limitations.

findings.evidence: GET /.env returned Vite HTTP 403 with no file contents. The missing content type belongs to a development-server deny response.
findings.impact: No secret exposure and no demonstrated product vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: No product change from this development-only response; retain denied access and verify deployed handling separately.
verification: Agent E manually reviewed the healthy isolated hosted-mode development instance on 2026-10-25.
See security/reports/runtime-assessment.md for scope, evidence and limitations.

notes: Only explicitly authorized exact origin requested; no redirects followed.
Reports omit raw bodies, cookies, authorization headers, secrets, and query strings.
Scanner alerts require manual validation; findings are not marked fixed by this wrapper.
Assessment target: http://127.0.0.1:3217, isolated Vite development instance, own local D1, dummy providers, no production/staging systems scanned.
All 22 metadata alerts manually triaged; same-endpoint CSP subrules and Nuclei/ZAP nosniff observations deduplicate in the aggregate registry.
Four runtime safety tests pass. No confirmed runtime application vulnerability or runtime application fix is claimed.
